title: recovery and replay: reconnecting workers replay unexpired undelivered messages without duplicating acknowledged content
fixture: tests/fixtures/swarm_v2/fleet-broadcasts.json: local seat eng-1@fixture and remote seat eng-2@fixture on channels brain and amygdala; operator critical warning acknowledged by generation 1, then a follow-up alert, an expired warning and an agent note published before the worker reconnects as generation 2 and claims at 61000 ms
fixture_clock: build() from tests/sv2_ctl02_cases.py patches time.time to the fixture clock and issues launch grants; FleetBroadcasts reads the same list; fakeredis server clock only in test_the_default_clock_is_the_redis_server_clock

state_assertions.replay: After the worker reconnects as generation 2 it receives the unexpired undelivered note and follow-up; the acknowledged warning and the expired warning are not replayed
state_assertions.operation_identity: Retrying claim-1 returns the same deliveries and leaves every broadcast key unchanged
state_assertions.fence: The older generation's claim and acknowledge raise stale_generation without writing
state_assertions.revision: A revised warning under op-1 becomes revision 2, an identical retry returns it, a retry with other content or lifetime is refused invalid_request; acknowledging revision 1 is refused stale_revision
state_assertions.until_ack: A delivered unacknowledged follow-up alert replays to the next generation with its first delivery time 1000 ms; an older generation's acknowledgement is refused stale_generation without writing

durability: Survived: canonical broadcasts, history, per-seat delivery records with generation and the operation map. Not covered: the local broadcast file, which a reconnecting worker rebuilds from claims
cleanup: fakeredis per test; no live resource mutations

broadcast_delivery_lag_seconds.dimension: seat eng-1@fixture; revision 2 published and claimed at 61000 ms; the follow-up replay keeps its first delivery time 1000 ms
